issues.legal_issue: Property acquired in the name of a joint-family member is presumed to be joint-family property only when the family had a sufficient nucleus at the time of acquisition.
material_facts: The acquisitions in dispute were made in the names of a family member’s wife, son, and grandson; the court found that the funds for several of them had been advanced by the family manager.

The evidence showed that family income had been substantially spent on family needs, cultivation, and other land purchases, and that the manager could have accumulated substantial savings from his separate earnings.
For acquisitions made when the son had long been earning independently, it was possible that he had used his own savings.
The court found no sufficient family nucleus available for the disputed acquisitions at the relevant times.
issues.conclusion: The disputed acquisitions were not shown to have been made from joint-family funds and were not liable to partition as joint-family property.
issues.legal_principle: Under the rule stated in Amritlal Sen & Ors. v. Surath Lal Sen, A.I.R. 1942 Cal. 553, and Appalaswami v. Suryanarayanamurthy & Ors., I.L.R. [1948] Mad. (P.C.) 440, property acquired in a joint-family member’s name is presumed to have been acquired from family funds, and to be joint-family property, if the family had a sufficient nucleus at the date of acquisition, unless the contrary is shown. The presumption therefore does not arise without a sufficient nucleus.

predicates.partition_suit: A family member brought a suit seeking division of alleged joint-family property.
predicates.property_acquired_in_member_name: The disputed property was acquired in the name of a member of the joint family or a member of that person’s branch.
predicates.family_nucleus_insufficient: The family’s available funds and income at the relevant acquisition time were not sufficient to provide a nucleus for the acquisition.
predicates.disputed_acquisitions_not_established_as: The disputed acquisitions are not treated as joint-family property liable to partition.

issues.definition: In a partition suit, acquisitions in a family member’s name are not established as joint-family property when the family lacked a sufficient nucleus at the time of acquisition.

issues.legal_issue: A joint-family manager is not required to account for past dealings in a partition suit when there is no evidence of fraud or misappropriation and the evidence shows no unexplained accumulation of family assets.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought an account of the manager’s past dealings with joint-family property and its income.
There was no evidence of fraud or misappropriation.
The evidence showed that family income had been spent and that the manager could not reasonably be expected to have accumulated funds beyond the family property identified for partition.
issues.conclusion: The manager was not required to render an account for past dealings before the demand for partition; the order refusing such an account was left undisturbed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Parameshwar Dube v. Govind Dube, I.L.R. 53 Cal. 459, absent fraud or other improper conduct, a joint-family manager’s account is directed to the existing state of property divisible at partition. The parties need not simply accept the manager’s statement about the property: the court should inquire into what property exists, using the usual method. Whether a further account is justified depends on the circumstances; where the evidence shows that no material accumulation could reasonably be expected, there is no justification for an account of past dealings.

predicates.partition_suit: A family member brought a suit seeking division of joint-family property and an account of its management.
predicates.no_evidence_of_fraud_or_misappropriation: The evidence did not show that the manager committed fraud or misappropriated family property or income.
predicates.no_unexplained_accumulation_expected: The evidence showed that the manager could not reasonably be expected to hold material accumulated family funds beyond the property identified for division.
predicates.manager_not_required_to_account_for_past: The manager is not required to render an account of past dealings with the family property.

issues.definition: In a partition suit, a manager need not account for past dealings when there is no evidence of fraud or misappropriation and no unexplained accumulation of family assets is reasonably expected.
